findings.title: CMEK and Kerberos-secret wiring is referentially correct but no IAM grant anywhere makes it actually usable
findings.explanation: The example wires google_kms_crypto_key.main into kms_key_name, google_kms_crypto_key.kerberos into kerberos_kms_key, google_secret_manager_secret_version.kerberos into kerberos_root_principal_password_uri, and a dedicated google_service_account.dataproc into gce_cluster_config.service_account — but nowhere in this repo is there a google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member/_binding granting the Cloud Dataproc Service Agent (service-{project}@dataproc-accounts.iam.gserviceaccount.com) roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on either key, a google_secret_manager_secret_iam_member granting that same agent roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor on the kerberos secret, or any google_project_iam_member granting google_service_account.dataproc roles/dataproc.worker. No single-resource rule can see this — it only shows up by following all four resources together. Each piece individually looks like a correct CMEK/Kerberos setup (which is exactly why HLD_GCP_150/151 pass), but as wired the cluster cannot actually create: GCP will reject encryption_config/kerberos_config for lack of KMS/secret access, and cluster nodes can't run without dataproc.worker. In practice this pushes whoever hits the apply failure toward the fastest fix under pressure — granting the service agent a broad role or loosening the key's IAM policy — rather than the narrow grant actually needed.
findings.remediation: Add google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member (role = "roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter") for both keys, a google_secret_manager_secret_iam_member (role = "roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor") for the kerberos secret, both scoped to the Dataproc Service Agent (data.google_project.current.number can build the service-{number}@dataproc-accounts.iam.gserviceaccount.com identity), and a google_project_iam_member granting google_service_account.dataproc roles/dataproc.worker. If these grants are intentionally managed in a separate IAM/bootstrap repo (the same pattern already used for this repo's WIF setup per provider.google.tf's holden:ignore comment), this finding doesn't apply — but that isn't verifiable from this repo alone, hence medium confidence.

findings.title: Dataproc cluster has no software_config.image_version, so the OS/component image is whatever GCP considers "latest" on the day of creation or recreation
findings.explanation: cluster_config has no software_config block at all. Dataproc resolves an unset image_version to the current default image at cluster creation time — the same non-determinism as image:latest in a container: two applies of the identical Terraform months apart can provision different, unvalidated OS/component versions, and any change that forces node recreation (e.g. a machine-type or network change) silently picks up whatever the new default is on that day rather than the version that was originally tested.
findings.remediation: Pin cluster_config.software_config.image_version to a specific Dataproc image (e.g. "2.2-debian12"), sourced from a variable so callers can control their own upgrade cadence deliberately instead of inheriting it implicitly.

findings.title: Example's Secret Manager rotation block is invalid HCL for this provider version and will fail terraform/tofu apply
findings.explanation: This is a plain apply-time correctness bug, not a security gap — noted here because it surfaced while tracing the Kerberos wiring for HOLDEN_AI_001 above, and belongs in this report's blind-spot category rather than being silently skipped. `tofu validate` on this directory fails with '"rotation": all of `rotation,topics` must be specified' — the google provider requires a `topics` argument (a Pub/Sub topic to notify) whenever `rotation_period` is set, and none is declared here. Separately, `next_rotation_time = timeadd(timestamp(), "2592000s")` re-evaluates timestamp() on every plan, so even once `topics` is added this attribute will show a perpetual diff on every run rather than converging.
findings.remediation: Either add a google_pubsub_topic + topics = [google_pubsub_topic.x.id] to complete the rotation block (and replace next_rotation_time with a static timestamp string, updated deliberately rather than derived from timestamp()), or drop the rotation block entirely if rotation is genuinely handled out-of-band as the secret_version's placeholder comment states.

suggested_policies.rationale: An unset software_config.image_version is the Dataproc equivalent of an unpinned/:latest container image — non-deterministic across applies and across forced recreation, with no record of what OS/component version was actually validated. This is a concrete, unambiguous not_null check with no legitimate reason to omit it deliberately (a caller who genuinely wants GCP's rolling default can still set image_version to a tracking alias if one exists, or the check can be suppressed per-resource via holden:ignore).
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: HLD_PROPOSED_001
name: Dataproc clusters should pin an explicit image_version
principle: supply-chain
severity: LOW
rationale: |
  A Dataproc cluster with no cluster_config.software_config.image_version
  resolves to whatever GCP considers the current default image at creation
  (or recreation) time. This is non-deterministic: two applies of identical
  Terraform at different times, or a change that forces node replacement,
  can silently provision a different, unvalidated OS/component image than
  the one originally tested.
remediation: |
  Add an explicit image_version:
    cluster_config {
      software_config {
        image_version = "2.2-debian12"
      }
    }
resources:
  google_dataproc_cluster:
    path: cluster_config.software_config.image_version
    not_null: true
